doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Taunts, sexuality and his mother's strictness
summary: He ignored rumors about Everybody's Somebody's Fool and says his mother's strictness shaped him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I guess what I was thinking was, in the case of Lester Young and Mingus, two of the most highly individual people in the history of jazz, getting kicked in the ass by them early on and still maintaining your integrity, I think is impressive, to me. The other thing I wanted to ask you was, the other challenges of your life – we’ve touched on the women. We’ve touched on the career – but the other challenges – I remember the story that went around about you, when Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool came out, and people were saying, “That’s not a man. That’s a lesbian in drag.” Jimmy, you must have heard those stories. Did you hear those stories? Or not?
Yeah but, again, like I say, you ignore it . . .

. . . and move on. You have to move on. You can’t let those things stop you. You hear them, and you are disappointed that it’s being said, but that’s just a disappointment, and you ignore it. You learn to ignore it. The main thing is, you don’t want it a part of your life. You don’t want it a part of your life. So you learn how to ignore those things when they come about.
So you don’t feel as though you had been taunted more than you could take. You felt as though you were equipped to handle the taunts and handle the teasing.
Yes. Exactly. I never had a confusion with a person about things like that.
I see. So sexually, you always knew who you were . . .

My mother was very strict with my brother and I about, “Get up boy. Stand up there.” You don’t drop down to other people’s things. No. You don’t do that. She was very strict about that. Yeah. And if I see her, she’s saying, “If I catch you ever, I’d tear your butt up.” And she would have.
Do you mean by that, catch you with a man? Or just catch you . . .?
Oh, anything derogative in life. “If I catch it, you going to get it.” That’s what that – that was her slogan. That’s her way. I didn’t want to get it, so I didn’t drop down to it.
